channel.title: The Drill Down: Baltimore Ravens
channel.description: Weekly NFL matchup scouting reports and win probabilities.

item.title: Week 12: Ravens at Texans
item.description: Sun 11/29 · 1:00 PM ET | Line: HOU -6.5 · O/U 46.5 | Model HOU 63% vs. market 73% | The game turns on whether Houston keeps attacking deep to the right, where it throws on 19% of passes, and whether Baltimore's secondary can limit the +0.40 EPA per throw it allows there. Mark Andrews creates 3.6 yards of separation against a Houston pass defense ranked 15th, and Brissett will need him open on time. Our model has Houston at 63%, below the market's 73%, and the starting quarterback spot drives most of that lean.

item.title: Week 11: Ravens at Panthers
item.description: Sun 11/22 · 1:00 PM ET | Line: CAR -2.5 · O/U 43.5 | Model CAR 53% vs. market 57% | Baltimore needs chunk plays to beat a Carolina defense that ranks 4th in explosive plays allowed, and the Ravens' offense ranks 27th in creating them. Tetairoa McMillan draws 33% of Carolina's air yards, and Baltimore's 19th-ranked pass defense will decide whether that volume becomes production. Our model has Carolina at 53% against the market's 57%, and home field is the main factor pushing us that way.

item.title: Week 10: Chargers at Ravens
item.description: Mon 11/16 · 8:15 PM ET | Line: BAL -4.5 · O/U 38.5 | Model BAL 88% vs. market 66% | The Chargers must generate chunk plays, a skill that ranks 29th in the league, against a Baltimore defense that allows explosives at the fifth-lowest rate. Mark Andrews has given back 2.0 yards after the catch versus expected, and the Chargers allow the 18th-most yards after catch over expected. Our model has Baltimore at 88 percent against a market price of 66, with the rushing matchup and the starting quarterback driving most of the gap.
